title: Public Service security legislative and policy framework
summary: Apply the correct legal and policy source to a departmental information decision.
outcomes: Distinguish legislation, directives, policy and voluntary guidance.
Reconcile privacy, access and records obligations.
Translate obligations into accountable service and supplier requirements.

realExample.title: The Information Regulator's security-compromise reporting portal
realExample.documentedOutcome: The Regulator introduced its eServices route for reporting security compromises from 1 April 2025.
realExample.discussion: A reporting obligation needs an operational channel, authorised people and a record of what was submitted. Use the portal transition to examine how a department updates an incident procedure when the receiving process changes.
realExample.scope: A documented regulatory service change. Availability of the portal does not itself prove departmental compliance.

units.title: Read the authority before choosing the control
objectives: Classify the authority of a source.
Explain the interaction of privacy, access and records.

chapters.title: An authority map prevents the wrong rule
chapters.bodyHtml:
Begin an obligation record with its issuing authority, exact title, version, relevant provision, scope and effective date. The Constitution protects privacy and access to information. Acts such as POPIA and PAIA give specific legal effect to relevant rights and responsibilities. A ministerial directive and a departmental policy have different authority from an optional technical guide.

Do not treat a draft bill, an old presentation or a vendor checklist as current law. A standard may become binding through a valid directive, contract or departmental adoption; its commercial popularity alone does not create that status. Keep the route by which it applies visible.

Use the register to connect an obligation to a service, owner, implemented measure and evidence. Record uncertainty as a question for the appropriate legal or policy owner, with a decision date. This is more useful than pasting legislation into a long document without explaining who must act.

chapters.title: Privacy and access require reasoned decisions
chapters.bodyHtml:
POPIA requires appropriate technical and organisational safeguards for personal information. The department needs to understand its processing purpose, risks and safeguards rather than assuming a consent checkbox resolves every issue. A DISO supplies security facts; the responsible privacy and legal roles determine the applicable processing basis and other legal requirements.

PAIA provides an access process with statutory grounds and procedures. A confidential label is not, by itself, a complete response to a lawful access request. Refer the request to the designated Information Officer process, preserve the record and provide the facts needed to assess disclosure, redaction and applicable exceptions.

The same dataset can therefore require protection against unauthorised viewing while also being subject to a properly considered access request. The practical task is to identify authorised purpose and process. Indiscriminate publication and indiscriminate refusal both avoid that decision.

chapters.title: Retention is part of protection
chapters.bodyHtml:
Government records include recorded information regardless of medium. NARSSA's guidance connects electronic records to an integrated records-management programme and written disposal authority. A scan is another representation; it does not automatically authorise destruction of the original.

Build a retention decision with the records owner: record series, purpose, applicable schedule or disposal authority, trigger date, required holds, approved disposal method and proof. Privacy-driven minimisation should be implemented with legal retention and archival duties, not by deleting evidence that the department is required to preserve.

During a dispute or incident, identify which records must remain available and how access is limited. Separate preservation from unrestricted use. A restricted retained copy can support an investigation without permitting routine browsing or creating uncontrolled copies.

application.title: Build an obligations register for a permit service
application.instructionsHtml:
Fictional case: Umzali Department is moving permit applications to an online platform. The supplier asks to keep all submissions indefinitely for product research. A journalist requests historical decision records. Records staff say an approved disposal schedule exists.

Spend about 60 minutes preparing five obligations-register entries and a decision route for the supplier request and journalist's request.
application.deliverable: A five-row register with source, scope, owner, measure and evidence.
application.suggestedAnswerHtml:
Include privacy safeguards and processing purpose, the PAIA request route, records retention/disposal authority, the departmental security directive and supplier contract requirements.

Do not approve research reuse merely because the supplier hosts the service. Obtain the actual purpose and legal assessment through the responsible roles. Route the access request for a statutory decision while preserving responsive records.

Use the actual schedule, not an invented universal retention period. The register should name a measure and evidence for each obligation.

reflection.prompt: Which policy in your environment is frequently described as law even though its authority has not been checked?
reflection.guidanceHtml: Identify the exact source and how you would establish its current scope before applying it.

quiz.title: Read the authority before choosing the control — knowledge check

questions.name: M02-U01-Q01
questions.promptHtml: Which entry gives the strongest basis for an obligation?

answers.textHtml: Exact source, provision, version and applicable scope
answers.feedbackHtml: Trace the requirement to its actual authority.

answers.textHtml: The latest departmental slide deck without its underlying authority or scope
answers.feedbackHtml: A secondary summary may omit qualifications and cannot establish the complete obligation.

answers.textHtml: A supplier's certificate without identifying the processing to which it applies
answers.feedbackHtml: A certificate alone does not define the department's obligations.

answers.textHtml: A policy title matched to a keyword without checking its current status
answers.feedbackHtml: Titles do not establish applicability, version or force.

questions.generalFeedbackHtml: Trace the requirement to its actual authority.

questions.name: M02-U01-Q02
questions.promptHtml: A record is labelled confidential and a PAIA request arrives. What should happen?

answers.textHtml: Preserve it and use the Information Officer's statutory request process
answers.feedbackHtml: Apply the statutory process and relevant grounds.

answers.textHtml: Refuse automatically because the departmental label says confidential
answers.feedbackHtml: A classification label does not replace the statutory request assessment.

answers.textHtml: Release automatically because the requester cited PAIA
answers.feedbackHtml: The statutory process includes the applicable grounds and responsibilities.

answers.textHtml: Let the document's technical custodian decide without the authorised request route
answers.feedbackHtml: Custody does not automatically confer the Information Officer's statutory decision role.

questions.generalFeedbackHtml: Apply the statutory process and relevant grounds.

questions.name: M02-U01-Q03
questions.promptHtml: A supplier says an ISO certificate eliminates every POPIA obligation. What is the best response?

answers.textHtml: Assess the actual processing and safeguards against the applicable obligations
answers.feedbackHtml: Certification may support assurance but does not decide every obligation.

answers.textHtml: Accept the certificate as satisfying all legal duties for every processing purpose
answers.feedbackHtml: Certification scope and legal obligations are not interchangeable.

answers.textHtml: Reject the certificate without considering its actual scope as supporting evidence
answers.feedbackHtml: A certificate can inform assessment even though it is not a complete substitute.

answers.textHtml: Check only the certificate expiry date and omit actual departmental processing
answers.feedbackHtml: Currency is relevant, but purpose, scope and safeguards also matter.

questions.generalFeedbackHtml: Certification may support assurance but does not decide every obligation.

questions.name: M02-U01-Q04
questions.promptHtml: What does digitising a paper record automatically authorise?

answers.textHtml: No automatic destruction of the original
answers.feedbackHtml: Check the records schedule and disposal authority.

answers.textHtml: Destruction as soon as the scanner reports a successful job
answers.feedbackHtml: Scanning does not supply the required disposal authority.

answers.textHtml: Destruction whenever a digital copy is easier for staff to search
answers.feedbackHtml: Convenience does not determine lawful records disposal.

answers.textHtml: Destruction after a local manager signs a generic scan-completion form
answers.feedbackHtml: A generic completion approval does not replace the applicable schedule, authority and preservation duties.

questions.generalFeedbackHtml: Check the records schedule and disposal authority.

questions.name: M02-U01-Q05
questions.promptHtml: A draft bill describes a proposed requirement. How should it be recorded?

answers.textHtml: As a proposal, with current applicable law identified separately
answers.feedbackHtml: Distinguish proposed changes from current authority.

answers.textHtml: As a current requirement solely because the consultation period has closed
answers.feedbackHtml: Closure of consultation does not establish enactment or commencement.

answers.textHtml: As an enacted rule because a professional newsletter summarised it
answers.feedbackHtml: A secondary summary does not change the proposal's legal status.

answers.textHtml: As a replacement for the current law before its adoption and commencement are established
answers.feedbackHtml: Current obligations remain separately identifiable.

questions.generalFeedbackHtml: Distinguish proposed changes from current authority.

questions.name: M02-U01-Q06
questions.promptHtml: What turns an obligations register into operating work?

answers.textHtml: A named owner, implemented measure and evidence for each requirement
answers.feedbackHtml: Connect the obligation to an accountable control.

answers.textHtml: Copying long passages without interpretation
answers.feedbackHtml: That does not allocate the work.

answers.textHtml: Removing dates to avoid updates
answers.feedbackHtml: Currency is essential.

answers.textHtml: Using one generic 'compliant' label for everything
answers.feedbackHtml: It hides scope and unresolved issues.

questions.generalFeedbackHtml: Connect the obligation to an accountable control.

questions.name: M02-U01-Q07
questions.promptHtml: Which two inputs belong in a retention decision? Select all correct answers.

answers.textHtml: The applicable records schedule or disposal authority
answers.feedbackHtml: This establishes the authorised route.

answers.textHtml: Relevant investigation or litigation preservation requirements
answers.feedbackHtml: They can affect whether disposal may proceed.

answers.textHtml: An arbitrary universal thirty-day period
answers.feedbackHtml: The scenario provides no such rule.

answers.textHtml: The supplier's desire to reuse everything
answers.feedbackHtml: Commercial preference is not retention authority.

questions.generalFeedbackHtml: Retention needs a source and context.

questions.name: M02-U01-Q08
questions.promptHtml: Which statements correctly distinguish source types? Select all correct answers.

answers.textHtml: A ministerial directive has an issuing authority and defined scope
answers.feedbackHtml: Its application must be read.

answers.textHtml: A technical guide can inform a control without becoming an Act
answers.feedbackHtml: Good practice and legislation are distinct.

answers.textHtml: Every standard is automatically a South African statute
answers.feedbackHtml: That is incorrect.

answers.textHtml: A draft consultation text is always already in force
answers.feedbackHtml: Its status must be checked.

questions.generalFeedbackHtml: Record how each source applies.

questions.name: M02-U01-Q09
questions.promptHtml: Protecting a record against unauthorised access can coexist with a lawful access-request process.
questions.trueFeedbackHtml: Protection and statutory access address different authorised circumstances.
questions.falseFeedbackHtml: This is incorrect. Protection and statutory access address different authorised circumstances.
questions.generalFeedbackHtml: Protection and statutory access address different authorised circumstances.

questions.name: M02-U01-Q10
questions.promptHtml: A data-retention policy can be set without considering records-management obligations.
questions.trueFeedbackHtml: This is incorrect. Retention and authorised disposal must be reconciled with applicable requirements.
questions.falseFeedbackHtml: Retention and authorised disposal must be reconciled with applicable requirements.
questions.generalFeedbackHtml: Retention and authorised disposal must be reconciled with applicable requirements.

questions.name: M02-U01-Q11
questions.promptHtml: Match the source to its principal course use.
questions.generalFeedbackHtml: These sources interact but are not interchangeable.

questions.name: M02-U01-Q12
questions.promptHtml: Record an obligation's issuing [[1]] and applicable [[2]] before adopting a measure.
questions.generalFeedbackHtml: Authority and scope establish why the requirement applies.

units.title: Make legal obligations usable in projects and incidents
objectives: Maintain a current compliance decision record.

chapters.title: Translate requirements into a service agreement
chapters.bodyHtml:
A supplier agreement should make the proposed processing understandable: information categories, purpose, authorised users, locations, subcontracting, security responsibilities, incident contact, return and disposal. Ask how the department can obtain evidence and recover its information if the relationship ends.

POPIA's operator provisions require attention to the written contract and security measures. A supplier may perform technical work while the department remains responsible for its own processing decisions. The DISO should provide assessable security requirements, with legal and procurement owners completing the agreement within their mandates.

Specify outcomes rather than unsupported assurances. For example, require named administrative access and retrievable access records for the relevant service, not simply 'enterprise-grade security'. Confirm that a receiving owner can check the requirement and that the service can continue during a dispute or exit.

chapters.title: Notification is an operational decision with a legal basis
chapters.bodyHtml:
Where the statutory trigger is met, POPIA section 22 requires the responsible party to notify the Regulator and affected data subjects, subject to its provisions, as soon as reasonably possible after discovery. Do not substitute a blanket imported 72-hour rule for that wording. The operator's duty to notify the responsible party immediately is a distinct step.

An incident record should preserve discovery time, what information may be affected, the basis for believing unauthorised access occurred, containment steps, decision makers and notification progress. Investigative uncertainty should be explained and updated; it should not be silently converted into certainty or used as an indefinite delay.

The Regulator's eServices channel introduced from 1 April 2025 is a concrete reason to review the procedure. Confirm authorised staff can use the current route and retain submission references. Provide affected people with clear, useful information through the appropriate process, while limiting unnecessary further disclosure.

chapters.title: Manage changes in authority and context
chapters.bodyHtml:
Compliance work changes when a service adds a dataset, a supplier changes processing, a new directive takes effect or a reporting channel changes. Keep a short change record: previous requirement, new source, affected services, owner, implementation date and evidence.

Review the actual contract and service before deciding whether a change is minor. Moving support to another country, adding analytics reuse or opening a new interface may change privacy, records and security questions even if the software screen looks the same.

Give management a decision they can assess: what changed, what remains uncertain, options, cost and service consequences. Preserve the advice and decision with their date and source version. Later reviewers should be able to understand why the department acted on the information available at the time.

application.title: Respond to a supplier disclosure and a changed purpose
application.instructionsHtml:
A fictional hosting supplier reports that an unauthorised support user downloaded applicant records yesterday. It offers to investigate for a month before telling anyone. Its renewal also adds a right to train its commercial analytics product on the records.

Spend about 60 minutes drafting an incident decision log and five contract questions. Identify the responsible-party/operator distinction and the current notification route.
application.deliverable: An incident log, notification work allocation and contract question list.
application.suggestedAnswerHtml:
Record known times, dataset and access facts, containment, unresolved scope and the legal/privacy decision owner. Assess the actual section 22 trigger promptly through that owner rather than accepting a supplier's one-month blanket delay.

The supplier's notification to the department is distinct from the responsible party's Regulator/data-subject duties. Prepare the current eServices submission and retained reference where required.

Treat analytics reuse as a separate purpose requiring assessment. Ask about authority, minimisation, access, onward processing and return/disposal; do not approve it through silence in a renewal.

reflection.prompt: Could your department identify who is authorised to submit a security-compromise notification during an absence?
reflection.guidanceHtml: Describe a practical deputy/access arrangement and how the submission reference would be retained.

quiz.title: Make legal obligations usable in projects and incidents — knowledge check

questions.name: M02-U02-Q01
questions.promptHtml: Which description best represents POPIA section 22 timing?

answers.textHtml: As soon as reasonably possible after discovery, applying the section's provisions
answers.feedbackHtml: Use the applicable statutory wording and documented circumstances.

answers.textHtml: A universal fixed seventy-two-hour deadline imported from another jurisdiction
answers.feedbackHtml: POPIA section 22 has its own timing and provisions.

answers.textHtml: Only after every forensic question has been resolved
answers.feedbackHtml: The notification assessment should not wait for unnecessary final certainty.

answers.textHtml: Only when the department renews the operator's contract
answers.feedbackHtml: Contract timing does not define the statutory notification duty.

questions.generalFeedbackHtml: Use the applicable statutory wording and documented circumstances.

questions.name: M02-U02-Q02
questions.promptHtml: Who does an operator notify under the distinct immediate-notification duty?

answers.textHtml: The responsible party
answers.feedbackHtml: Operator-to-responsible-party notification is distinct from the responsible party's duties.

answers.textHtml: Only the Information Regulator, leaving the responsible party uninformed
answers.feedbackHtml: The distinct operator duty is immediate notification to the responsible party.

answers.textHtml: Only the affected data subjects, without notifying the responsible party
answers.feedbackHtml: This confuses the operator's duty with the responsible party's statutory assessment and notifications.

answers.textHtml: Only the operator's internal incident committee until it completes a final report
answers.feedbackHtml: An internal process does not replace the immediate notification duty.

questions.generalFeedbackHtml: Operator-to-responsible-party notification is distinct from the responsible party's duties.

questions.name: M02-U02-Q03
questions.promptHtml: Which supplier requirement is assessable?

answers.textHtml: Named administrative access with retrievable service access records
answers.feedbackHtml: Specify a condition and how its owner can verify it.

answers.textHtml: A general promise to use industry-leading security without defined scope
answers.feedbackHtml: An undefined quality claim is difficult to assess against an operating result.

answers.textHtml: A certificate described as covering all future departmental uses automatically
answers.feedbackHtml: The future scope and actual controls still require assessment.

answers.textHtml: An obligation to provide access records only if the supplier chooses to retain them
answers.feedbackHtml: The department needs a clear retrievable-record responsibility rather than a discretionary promise.

questions.generalFeedbackHtml: Specify a condition and how its owner can verify it.

questions.name: M02-U02-Q04
questions.promptHtml: A renewal adds analytics reuse of applicant records. What should the department do?

answers.textHtml: Assess the changed purpose and authority before accepting it
answers.feedbackHtml: Review the actual proposed processing, not just the screen.

answers.textHtml: Assume hosting permission covers any reuse
answers.feedbackHtml: Purposes and roles need examination.

answers.textHtml: Ignore it because the user interface is unchanged
answers.feedbackHtml: Processing can change without a visible interface change.

answers.textHtml: Delete the contract history
answers.feedbackHtml: History is needed to understand the change.

questions.generalFeedbackHtml: Review the actual proposed processing, not just the screen.

questions.name: M02-U02-Q05
questions.promptHtml: Why retain a notification submission reference?

answers.textHtml: To link the decision and content to the actual receiving event
answers.feedbackHtml: Preserve both decision context and provider receipt.

answers.textHtml: To establish that the Regulator approved every departmental decision in the notice
answers.feedbackHtml: Receipt is not the same as substantive approval.

answers.textHtml: To replace the underlying incident and notification records
answers.feedbackHtml: The reference links to those records rather than replacing them.

answers.textHtml: To conclude that no subsequent correction or further information can be needed
answers.feedbackHtml: An initial receipt does not settle all later obligations.

questions.generalFeedbackHtml: Preserve both decision context and provider receipt.

questions.name: M02-U02-Q06
questions.promptHtml: What should a legal-change record include?

answers.textHtml: Affected service, source version, owner and implementation evidence
answers.feedbackHtml: The record supports a traceable operational change.

answers.textHtml: Only the publication date and URL, with no affected service or owner
answers.feedbackHtml: A source reference needs an implementation link to become actionable.

answers.textHtml: Only an undated completion label without the implemented change
answers.feedbackHtml: The record must explain what was done and against which version.

answers.textHtml: One generic entry assumed to apply identically to every service
answers.feedbackHtml: Applicability and operating effects can differ by service.

questions.generalFeedbackHtml: The record supports a traceable operational change.

questions.name: M02-U02-Q07
questions.promptHtml: Which facts help a notification assessment? Select all correct answers.

answers.textHtml: Discovery time and basis for believing unauthorised access occurred
answers.feedbackHtml: These inform the actual trigger and timing.

answers.textHtml: Known information scope and containment steps
answers.feedbackHtml: These support useful, accurate reporting.

answers.textHtml: A fabricated exact count to look decisive
answers.feedbackHtml: Unknowns must remain explicit.

answers.textHtml: The supplier's desire to avoid publicity as a complete legal reason
answers.feedbackHtml: Commercial preference does not decide the duty.

questions.generalFeedbackHtml: Record known facts and assess uncertainty through the proper roles.

questions.name: M02-U02-Q08
questions.promptHtml: Which agreement terms support usable supplier governance? Select all correct answers.

answers.textHtml: Information return and exit responsibilities
answers.feedbackHtml: They support continuity and retained ownership.

answers.textHtml: Incident contacts and evidence access
answers.feedbackHtml: They make response responsibilities workable.

answers.textHtml: Unlimited undisclosed reuse by default
answers.feedbackHtml: That leaves processing scope uncontrolled.

answers.textHtml: No departmental access to its own records
answers.feedbackHtml: That creates an unacceptable service dependency.

questions.generalFeedbackHtml: Make responsibilities and recovery routes explicit.

questions.name: M02-U02-Q09
questions.promptHtml: A changed reporting channel can require an incident-procedure update even when the underlying Act is unchanged.
questions.trueFeedbackHtml: Operational compliance includes reaching the current receiving route.
questions.falseFeedbackHtml: This is incorrect. Operational compliance includes reaching the current receiving route.
questions.generalFeedbackHtml: Operational compliance includes reaching the current receiving route.

questions.name: M02-U02-Q10
questions.promptHtml: A supplier's statement that it is compliant automatically transfers all departmental responsibility to it.
questions.trueFeedbackHtml: This is incorrect. Supplier performance and departmental accountability remain distinct.
questions.falseFeedbackHtml: Supplier performance and departmental accountability remain distinct.
questions.generalFeedbackHtml: Supplier performance and departmental accountability remain distinct.

questions.name: M02-U02-Q11
questions.promptHtml: Match the record to the question it answers.

pairs.answer: How information and service leave the supplier

questions.generalFeedbackHtml: A complete operating record connects purpose, events and continuity.

questions.name: M02-U02-Q12
questions.promptHtml: A changed processing [[1]] requires a fresh assessment of its applicable [[2]].
questions.generalFeedbackHtml: A new purpose is a substantive governance change.
